prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on what you want to do in Branson.

Quick guide to choose
- Stay in a hotel if you want convenience, predictable service/cleaning, on‑site amenities (pool, breakfast, concierge), or if you're attending shows on the 76 Strip and want walkability. Hotels are easier for short stays, business trips, and families who want fewer logistics.
- Stay in an Airbnb/cabin if you want more space, a kitchen, privacy, lake access or a hot tub, or you’re traveling with a larger group. Cabins around Table Rock Lake or a rental near Silver Dollar City are great for nature, boating, and quieter evenings.

Best neighborhoods by purpose
- 76 Country Boulevard (the “Strip”): closest to theaters, dinner shows, shopping, and nightlife. Good for hotels and condos if you want to be in the center of the action.
- Branson Landing (lakefront downtown on Lake Taneycomo): nicer restaurants, lakewalk, shops — good balance of walkability and quieter evenings.
- Table Rock Lake / Indian Point / Kimberling City / Hollister: lake cabins and Airbnbs — best for boating, fishing, scenic relaxation.
- Branson West / near Silver Dollar City: pick this area for easy access to Silver Dollar City and quieter rental cabins.
- Big Cedar / Ridgedale area: upscale resort experience with outdoor activities nearby.

Specific properties / types to consider
Hotels (good for convenience, families, show-goers)
- Chateau on the Lake Resort, Spa & Convention Center — luxury lakeside resort with marina and spa.
- Big Cedar Lodge (resort) — higher-end Ozarks resort with cabins, activities, great if you want a resort experience.
- Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing — right on Branson Landing for dining/shopping walkability.
- Drury Plaza Hotel Branson (near Hwy 76) — reliable mid-range with good breakfast/pool; convenient to shows.
- Hilton Branson Convention Center — handy if you want a larger hotel with lots of services.

Airbnbs / cabins (best for groups, lake time, privacy)
- Lakefront or lake‑view cabins on Table Rock Lake (search Indian Point, Kimberling City, Hollister) — look for private dock, hot tub, and ample sleeping space.
- Cabins within 15–20 minutes of Silver Dollar City if the theme park is your focus.
- Condos or short‑term rentals at Branson Landing if you want walkable dining and lake views.
- Big private homes or multi‑cabin Airbnbs for reunions — many in the Table Rock/Lakeside area.

Booking tips & what to check
- If you want shows/restaurants: book on/near the 76 Strip or Branson Landing.
- If you want boating/lake time: verify dock privileges, parking for trailers, and water access.
- Read recent reviews (last 6–12 months) for cleanliness/noise and host responsiveness.
- For Airbnbs: check cancellation policy, exact location (some are on steep rural roads), heating/AC, cell/internet coverage.
- For hotels: watch for weekend rate surges (shows/peak season). Look for free breakfast, parking, and pool if those matter.
- Book early for summer and fall (popular seasons) and holiday weekends.

If you tell me: dates, group size, budget, and top priorities (shows vs lake vs family vs quiet), I can give 3–5 tailored listings (hotels and cabins) and find the best neighborhood for your stay.
